clue.text: Arguing continued before stopping

parts.note: stopping, as a noun, is an ending

explanation.surface: Someone kept up a row right up until the moment they stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Contending is disputing a point, a synonym of arguing.

clue.text: Love friend, providing a precious stone

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A lover and a friend give each other a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: Very sad time with smoke going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word for smoke is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cigar is something you smoke

explanation.surface: A sorrowful moment as smoke rises, perhaps from a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'going up' turns the smoke word to read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes a calamity, something deeply distressing.

clue.text: No big charges in this day care centre

definitions.text: No big charges in this day care centre

parts.words: No big charges in this day care centre
parts.note: the charges are not fees but the little ones in someone's charge, small children looked after during the day

explanation.surface: A childcare place advertising that it does not charge much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' reads as fees; it means children placed in someone's care, who are certainly not big.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young children are minded by day.

clue.text: I run on into club

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone jogs onward and into a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a type of golf club.

clue.text: Fuel, half a gallon, to get across London area

indicators.note: the shortened gallon stretches across, enclosing, the London district
half of the word gallon means its first three letters are kept

parts.note: Soho is a district of central London

explanation.surface: Someone takes half a gallon of fuel to drive across part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first three letters of 'gallon'. Soho is an entertainment district in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasohol is a motor fuel blending petrol with alcohol.

clue.text: Instrument of torture provided by little Tom's bunch

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of a folk tale, so little Tom's is THUMB'S
a crew is a bunch of people

explanation.surface: A torture device supplied by a gang belonging to a small boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbscrews were a device for crushing the thumbs, used to extract confessions.

clue.text: One of the family ties?

parts.note: family ties suggests bonds of kinship, but read as a knot tied by an elderly relative

explanation.surface: A question about the bonds that hold a family together.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny knot is a badly tied reef knot, named after a grandmother.

clue.text: Most of the gold used to make god

indicators.note: most of the word the means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Most of the gold went into making an idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse deity of thunder.

clue.text: Soldiers made off with OAP's parrot

indicators.note: made off suggests escaping, read as the letters being made into something else

explanation.surface: Troops stole a pensioner's pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP is an old-age pensioner. The letters of OAPS and PARROT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroops are airborne soldiers dropped by parachute.

clue.text: Unregenerate nature of lord in Arab territory

indicators.note: the abbreviation for lord is placed within the name of the Arab state

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A nobleman's unreformed character shows in a Middle Eastern land.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Biblical sense: the 'old man' is sinful human nature before conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian usage the old man is sinful human nature not yet reborn.

clue.text: Performance — former jester's last in court

indicators.note: the former word and the jester's final letter are placed inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: once means formerly, in the past

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of jester

explanation.surface: A show given by a one-time court jester.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert is a musical performance.

clue.text: A miss by a whisker?

parts.note: a near miss, with a playful hint of a razor taking whiskers very close to the skin

explanation.surface: A question about only just missing something.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is an idiom for only just avoiding disaster.

clue.text: City in which you may see drunken man tonight

indicators.note: drunken signals the letters reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy man out on the town this evening in some city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Building that has a rope attached

definitions.meaning: a tall structure such as a castle keep
read as ..., something that tows with a rope

explanation.definitionFit: A tower is a tall structure; a tow-er is a vehicle hauling something by a line.

clue.text: Plant providing nectar across the street

indicators.note: the sweet word stretches across, enclosing, the abbreviation

parts.note: honey is often called nectar, sweet stuff

explanation.surface: A flower yields sweet nectar on the other side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty is a garden flower, Lunaria, with papery seed pods.

clue.text: Former PM in barren land

explanation.surface: An ex-premier found out on a moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath led Britain in the 1970s; heathland is open, uncultivated ground.

clue.text: Bumpkin lays down burden by lake

parts.note: a yoke is a burden or oppressive load

explanation.surface: A country lad sets down his load beside the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person.

clue.text: Kind leader goes to the end of the queue for leftovers

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for kind moves to the back, as in a queue

parts.note: a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: A gentleman at the front of the queue steps back to let others go for scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective; it means SORT, whose S then shifts to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps of food left after a meal.

clue.text: Architect gets the bird

definitions.meaning: Sir Christopher ..., designer of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A designer is jeered or dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' is slang for being booed, but here 'the bird' is the small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren designed St Paul's in London; the wren is a small songbird.

clue.text: Woman denied a bed

indicators.note: denied means the letter a is refused, taken away

parts.note: Bertha is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is refused somewhere to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a bunk on a ship or train.

clue.text: Fungus you found in France in tree trunks

indicators.note: the French word is placed within the word for tree trunks

parts.note: boles are tree trunks
tu is French for you

explanation.surface: A mushroom you discovered among French tree trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Boletus is a genus of mushrooms including the cep.

clue.text: Poor person in shelter with old books

parts.note: a haven is a shelter
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A pauper sits in a refuge with some ancient volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is someone lacking wealth, as opposed to the haves.

clue.text: Harsh landlord perhaps — English and 25

parts.note: the number points to the clue numbered 25, the surname of the French writer whose forename is Victor

explanation.surface: A cruel landlord, of English stock, linked to a numbered entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 answer is the surname of the novelist of Les Misérables; his first name supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor turns tenants out of their homes, as a harsh landlord might.

clue.text: Dope only 50% with it?

parts.note: fifty percent is a half

explanation.surface: A fool is only half as fashionable as he thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' reads as trendy, but splits into W for 'with' and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a stupid person, like a dope.

clue.text: Past device for giving something a shape

definitions.text: device for giving something a shape
definitions.meaning: a mould or tool that forms things

explanation.definitionFit: Former means earlier; a former is also a shaping tool or mould.

clue.text: Bargain brings delight, no end, to ugly old dame

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the delight word is removed

parts.note: glee is delight

explanation.surface: A deal makes a wizened crone happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bargain' is the verb, to haggle over a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to dispute a price, the verb sense of bargain.

clue.text: Boy needing cuddle and love

parts.note: a hug is a cuddle
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lad wants a cuddle and affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo is a boy's name.

clue.text: Woman making article one way and another

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the article is written forwards and then the other way round

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman producing a piece of writing by various means.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's name.

clue.text: Series of games has team not bad collecting ashes trophy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters gather the urn into their middle
bad signals the letters of team not are in a poor, jumbled state

parts.note: the Ashes cricket trophy is a tiny urn

explanation.surface: A sports competition where a not-bad side wins the Ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series, whose trophy is a small urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a contest made up of a series of matches.

clue.text: Meat placed in stove always

indicators.note: the letters are found placed within the words stove always

explanation.surface: Meat is always kept in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is calf meat.

clue.text: A biscuit — best hard or mushy?

indicators.note: mushy suggests the letters are squashed into a new form

explanation.surface: A question of whether a biscuit is better crunchy or soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich buttery Scottish biscuit.
